question: Not what could we buy, but what is already arriving that we throw away. A field we ignore cost exactly as much as a field we use.
blindSpots: Chat cannot reach the provider's documentation or make a live call. Everything here is read from responses already stored.
It can say what ARRIVED. It cannot say what an endpoint would return if asked differently — that needs somebody with a key.
It cannot see rate limits, quotas or tier boundaries; those are dashboard facts.

allocation.spend: ENRICHMENT on the top few thousand cards
allocation.buys: Sales VOLUME and graded sold prices. This is the only candidate that unlocks instruments we cannot build at all today - every number we publish currently reads asks and infers demand, and vol30 measures demand directly. It also unblocks the graded index and makes RT-5 testable for the first time.
allocation.why: Capability, not coverage. We already have prices on 16,468 cards and volume on twelve.

allocation.haveNow: 207 products, chosen by hand from eBay
allocation.buys: Coverage of a market nobody else indexes, on a catalogue we have never even counted. The endpoint exists and has only ever been queried by name.
allocation.why: Second because it widens something we already do well rather than enabling something new - but it is the widest gap between what we track and what exists.

allocation.spend: Twice-daily refresh on the top 500 cards and boxes
allocation.buys: Intraday movement on the things people actually watch. A $2,000 card can move meaningfully between breakfast and dinner.
allocation.why: Cheap, and the only way to say anything about a market DURING a day rather than about yesterday.

allocation.spend: Historical backfill where the provider has it
allocation.buys: Every thesis we hold reports INSUFFICIENT for want of history. Backfill would make RT-1, RT-3 and RT-7 testable years earlier than waiting.
allocation.why: Highest long-term value, entirely dependent on whether the provider exposes history at our tier - which nobody has checked.

findings.what: raw.recentSales arrives on every card and is never read
findings.why: what things actually SOLD for. We currently compare asks to prices and label the mismatch; sales would let us report the transaction instead of the intention.
findings.action: wire it through — the call is already being made and the data is already being paid for

findings.what: raw.vol30 arrives on every card and is never read
findings.why: actual 30-day sales VOLUME. Every instrument we own reads listings — asks — and infers demand from them. This is demand measured directly, and no competitor publishes it.
findings.action: wire it through — the call is already being made and the data is already being paid for

findings.what: ebaySold.psa9 arrives populated and is never read
findings.why: the other half of the PSA-9 tax thesis (RT-5), which is currently INSUFFICIENT for want of exactly this.
findings.action: wire it through - the call is already made and the data already paid for

findings.what: gradingPremium.psa9 arrives on every card and is never read
findings.why: the other half of the PSA-9 tax thesis (RT-5), which is currently INSUFFICIENT for want of exactly this.
findings.action: wire it through — the call is already being made and the data is already being paid for

findings.what: /sealed-products is only ever queried by name
findings.why: We ask it about products we already picked from somewhere else, so our universe is bounded by a list we wrote by hand rather than by what the provider actually holds.
findings.action: page through it once and count what is there — the answer changes what is possible, not just what is convenient

findings.what: 2 places fetch one item at a time inside a loop
findings.why: If any of those endpoints accept a batch or a set filter, we are spending N calls where one would do — and call budget is the thing that decides how much of the market we can see.
findings.action: check whether each endpoint supports a set, page or id-list parameter before scaling the loop up

findings.what: the paid provider is called from 83 places
findings.why: A paid tier justifies itself by what it uniquely provides. If the only thing we take from it is a price we could get free elsewhere, we are paying for a duplicate.
findings.action: list what ONLY the paid provider gives us; if that list is short, either use more of it or stop paying for it

findings.why: Spare capacity is not saved for anything - unspent calls do not roll over, so every day at 39% of budget is a day of capability we simply did not take.
findings.action: Spend it in the ranked order above: capability before coverage.
